cards.scientific_scope: New internal fixed-direction positivity/uniqueness and weak-dual extension, shear/product family coercivity and exact reduced-phase obstructions. No full invariant-cone quasiconvexity or historical originality claim.
cards.statement: For real rank-one-convex homogeneous quartic F with mu>0 and fixed planar n in W1,4, every positive-mass nonnegative amplitude minimum is attained, unique and strictly positive in the interior. Positive boundary or torus gives an attained L4/3 flux dual with L1 divergence and exact boundary pairing. Sheared theta=ky+g(x), k nonzero integer, and complex product maps satisfy E F(Du)>=mu/(1+2*cuberoot(3))^3 E|Du|4. Antipodal amplitude/factor symmetry extends the specified families to all affine backgrounds.
assumptions: Bounded connected Lipschitz planar domain or connected flat torus; real homogeneous quartic rank-one convexity with explicit strictly positive rank-one minimum mu; fixed direction n in W1,4 and admissible nonnegative amplitude trace.

Global unweighted weak-dual attainment requires torus or strictly positive continuous boundary amplitude. Zero boundary retains positivity/uniqueness but exact r=x example rules out this flux-class attainment.

proof_spine: Signed scalar variational minimum, density perspective, coercivity with rough L1 potential and logarithmic Morrey estimate give positivity; strict interpolation gives uniqueness.
Fenchel equality and Euler equation yield constant weak residual; nonzero boundary retains weak normal pairing. Mass-value is C1, no smooth optimal flux implied.

Exact common-boundary amplitude-minimized phase nonconvexity, false general averaging and failed determinant support/cubic-only estimates isolate the remaining global sign.
